done.why: I saw the opening and one strong encounter, then stopped early on my own. I did not reach an ending.

about: A cave-adventure sequel. You are tested in a shadowy underground land, and an old man in a dream tells you to seek him when you are worthy. You fight a hooded double of yourself and explore the passages.

moments.note: The parser answered 'You can't eat the lamp' when I said lantern. It quietly renamed the lantern to lamp.
The sword from the junction appeared in my hand when the hooded figure showed up.
Taking the hood showed my own face, which then aged and faded. It was a strong beat.
Climbing the stairs only gave 'The stairs are endless.' Talking to the old man gave 'can't see any such thing'.

wished: Talk to the old man from the dream
Read the runes on the sword
Find out what the stair is for

lines.line: You slowly remove the hood from your badly wounded opponent and recoil in horror at the sight of your own face, weary and wounded.
lines.why: This was the high point. The fight turned into a self-confrontation.

lines.line: It lowers its sword, and its head with it, and waits; the hood hangs within reach of your hand.
lines.why: The enemy offered itself, which was an odd and effective piece of staging.

fun.why: Short but with one memorable scene.

engagement.why: The setup pulled me forward. I stopped early.

difficulty.why: The fight was easy and I had no puzzles.

interestingness.why: The dream frame and the doppelganger gave it a clear theme.

prose.why: Sparse and evocative, with good atmosphere in the shadow land.
